ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG) of 10 October 1997, SR 955.0; Swiss Criminal Code Art. 305bis and 305ter, SR 311.0; Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 697j–697k (beneficial owner register of legal entities), SR 220; Ordinance on the Transparency of Legal Entities (Transparenzverordnung) of 22 June 2023; FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA), SR 955.033.0; FINMA Circular 2011/01; Federal Act on the Commercial Register and related ordinances (SR 221.41), governing UBO identification and disclosure to banks, fiduciaries, and authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential or business address (utility bill or lease agreement) of each UBO

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against: (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) Swiss SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) consolidated sanctions list and Swiss Ordinance on Measures against Money Laundering (SR 946.231.112); (iii) EU and UK HM Treasury consolidated financial sanctions lists (best practice aligned with FINMA expectations); (iv) OFAC SDN List for USD-corridor and correspondent banking compatibility; (v) Swiss PEP register and international PEP databases. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) applies to foreign and domestic PEPs and international organization functionaries per Art. 2a AMLA, including a 12-month post-cessation tail; screening is refreshed at onboarding, every six months, and upon any ownership change; negative findings must be documented in a compliance memo approved by the AML officer before notarization.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Swiss Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex, ZEFIX) at https://www.zefix.ch, operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office; preliminary name search also through cantonal commercial register offices (Handelsregisteramt) and the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be expressed in at least one Swiss official language (German, French, Italian, or Romansh) and written in Latin script (Arts. 950 and 951 of the Swiss Code of Obligations). The legal form suffix must appear as 'Aktiengesellschaft', 'AG', 'Société Anonyme', 'SA', or 'Società Anonima' / 'SA' depending on language of the articles. Foreign names require an official transliteration into Latin characters; the name must not be misleading and must correspond to the actual corporate purpose (web scraping, data aggregation, API commerce).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Provisional name reservation is valid for 30 days and may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon written justification and payment of the cantonal extension fee. Upon rejection, the applicant may: (i) request a written reasoned refusal from the competent cantonal commercial register office; (ii) file an administrative appeal with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority (Handelsregisteraufsichtsbehörde) within 30 days of service; (iii) on further failure, appeal to the Federal Administrative Court in St. Gallen within 30 days. The appeal must include the contested name, a proposed alternative, and statutory evidence of permissibility; appeal fees range from CHF 200 to CHF 1,000.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. The articles of association must designate a physical registered office in Switzerland (Art. 626 OR) and a mere P.O. Box or pure virtual address is not acceptable to cantonal commercial registers. However, a serviced office, co-working lease, or registered-agent arrangement with a physical address and a named person authorized to accept service of process is permissible. For the target web-scraping and API business, a serviced office in the economic zones of Zug, Zurich, or Geneva is acceptable subject to a written service agreement demonstrating physical presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-Medium: estimated 10–15% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 18 months for a non-regulated data-API business using a reputable serviced office; probability rises to approximately 25–35% where a mass virtual-office provider is used or where VAT registration triggers Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) site visits. Inspection authorities include the cantonal commercial register office, cantonal tax authorities, and ESTV.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft / Société Anonyme), specifically Arts. 626, 628, 632-634, 640, 642, and 643; Companies Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV) Arts. 6-16.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Kantonales Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) under supervision of the Federal Commercial Register Office (EHRA) in Bern
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif / Gründungsurkunde) and Articles of Incorporation (Statuts / Statuten)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000, split into fully paid registered shares; at least CHF 50,000 must be fully paid up in cash or in kind and placed in a blocked escrow account with a Swiss bank until registration is granted (OR Arts. 632-634; capital must be released after the Commercial Register certificate is issued).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the board of directors of [Company Name] AG hereby approves and takes unanimous action on the following matters: (1) The share subscription of the founders, totaling the fully paid-in share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 each, is accepted and ratified; (2) The registered office is established at [Address], [Postal Code], Switzerland; (3) The following officers are appointed: [Name] as Chief Executive Officer and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, each with full signatory authority; (4) The board authorizes the filing of these resolutions with the competent Commercial Register and any other authorities as required by law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (Office du notaire / Notariat of the registered office canton)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange personal or authorized-consular appearance before a Swiss notary public. Execute the deed of incorporation and approve the articles of association. The notary will certify the document and forward it to the Commercial Register. Ensure the shares, capital structure, and board mandate are consistent with the company's data-API purpose.
required_dossiers: Passport or identity document of each founder and beneficial owner
Draft Articles of Incorporation (in German, French, or Italian; certified translation where English is used)
Notarized power of attorney for any absent founder
Certificate of no criminal record for directors (excerpt from register of criminal sanctions if obtained via cantonal procedure)
Declaration of acceptance of office by directors and auditors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or register queries defects, correct and re-execute the deed within 10 days; supplementary notarizations may be issued without restarting the entire process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Capital Escrow and Bank Evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss licensed bank (e.g., UBS, Credit Suisse, Raiffeisen, or a recognized securities dealer)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-interest-bearing blocked capital account at a Swiss bank. Deposit at least CHF 50,000 in cash (or the full amount if in-kind capital is not used) and obtain a written confirmation of deposit from the bank stating the funds are freely available and blocked until the Commercial Register issuance is produced. The bank will release the funds after the Company Certificate is received.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation or proof of application
Final articles of association
Identification of beneficial owners (for AML verification)
Swiss tax residence certificate of the company (if pre-issued)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires further KYC documentation, promptly deliver updated ownership and source-of-funds explanations; Korean identifications and incorporation drafts are typically sufficient after the bank's AML team clears the file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Auditors or Statutory Waiver
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders' General Meeting; Federal Audit Oversight Authority (FAOA) for appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Unless all shareholders unanimously elect an 'opting-out' exemption from ordinary audit (appropriate for a company with fewer than 10 full-time employees and a balance sheet below CHF 500,000), the founders must appoint a licensed audit firm (Revisionsstelle). The company's data-API business frequently qualifies for a limited audit; the board passes a resolution appointing the auditor and authorizing signature.
required_dossiers: Auditor engagement letter signed by the audit firm
Declarations of independence from the audit firm
Shareholders' waiver for audit exemption (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the audit firm is declined by the register, call an extraordinary shareholders meeting to appoint another recognized auditor, correcting the filing without invalidating the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Filing and Official Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete notarized dossier to the Cantonal Commercial Register. The Register verifies legal compliance and statutory capital. Upon approval, the company obtains its Swiss Company Identification Number (UID) and the incorporation is published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt – SHAB). The registration is effective retroactively to the date the deed was signed.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and articles of association
Bank confirmation of blocked capital
Directors' and auditors' consents
Power of attorney for the applicant
Declaration of nominee directors (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The register may issue a formal request for clarification (e.g., translation or additional shareholder proof). Provide a response within 5 business days; otherwise the application lapses. A re-filing is permitted without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), Cantonal Tax Authority, AHV Compensation Office, and Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the UID extract is issued, register for VAT (obligatory if gross turnover exceeds CHF 100,000), register as an employer for AHV/IV/EO social insurance, and notify the cantonal tax authority for direct tax purposes. The scraping-API company may be considered a data controller; if so, complete the FDPIC data-processing register entry under the Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP).
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt with UID
Authorized signatory's passport copy
Employee records or declaration of no staff yet
Data-processing register extract for FADP if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late notifications can be made online through www.easyminadmin.ch or the ESTV portal after registration; a late-filing supplementation is generally accepted without fine if no taxable payroll has yet occurred.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – digital commerce and data-API services do not require an industrial license. For the operating head office, the municipal or cantonal trade authority (Amt für Wirtschaft / Office de l'économique) may require a simple business permit (polizeiliche Bewilligung) depending on the canton.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None (market freedom under the Swiss Code of Obligations); optional data protection registration with the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) is required if personal data is processed through the scraping API.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category 4 – non-industrial digital service, no physical manufacturing or hazardous processes). No EIA preparation needed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; nevertheless, the office must comply with Swiss waste management ordinances (VVEA) for IT equipment disposal and any municipal water discharge rules for cooling or sanitization, though digital API operations do not generate industrial wastewater or VOC emissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the cantonal fire prevention authority, structural load inspection for office premises, occupational health and safety validation under SUVA (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund), and workplace hygiene clearance by the cantonal labor inspectorate. For a remote API development team, a simple ergonomic IT workstation compliance check is sufficient.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (SFTA) / Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV), Portal: www.estv.admin.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must apply for a Swiss VAT number (MWST-Nummer) using SFTA Form 754 (registration for VAT purposes). If the entity is not domiciled in Switzerland but performs taxable activities in Switzerland, it must appoint a domestic tax representative or fiscal establishment. The application requires a copy of the commercial register excerpt, statutes, board resolution, and proof of anticipated turnover. Upon registration, the entity receives a Swiss UID number (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), which also serves as the tax identification number for all Swiss taxes. For entities not registered in the Swiss commercial register, a separate VAT ID is assigned.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide a 'check-the-box' election. An AG (Aktiengesellschaft) is automatically a separate taxable entity for federal, cantonal, and communal corporate income taxes and is subject to Swiss withholding tax on distributions. For VAT, an election for VAT grouping is available under Art. 21 Swiss VAT Act (Ortsbezogene Zusammenschlüsse, Gruppenbesteuerung). Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized; Switzerland applies domestic anti-hybrid rules consistent with OECD BEPS Action 2 only to the extent explicitly implemented.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 in annual global turnover (Art. 10 para. 2 VAT Act) for domestic entrepreneurs; for foreign entrepreneurs, registration is required when Swiss-source taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per year and the foreign business is not already exempt; voluntary registration is possible for smaller turnover. Special reduced threshold of CHF 25,000 applies to non-profit sports and charitable events.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance system (no CFDI/PEPPOL-style clearance mandate). However, the Swiss VAT Act requires definitive e-invoicing for audit trail purposes using Swiss QR-bill (ISO 20022) when invoicing by electronic means. For business-to-government (B2G) transactions, e-invoicing is mandatory for federal procurement since 2020. No API-based fiscal stamping is required by the SFTA; instead, taxpayers must retain original electronic records and provide access on request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0%) under Art. 18 and Art. 23 Swiss VAT Act applies to: (1) supplies of movable goods exported from Switzerland to a foreign country, provided the goods are physically transported out of Switzerland by the supplier, the buyer, or a third party; (2) supplies of services if the recipient is based abroad and the service is effectively used abroad, with limited exclusions for immovable property, goods-related services, and passenger transport; (3) transport services and other services directly related to exported goods. Advance rulings are available for ambiguous cases; the zero rate must be substantiated with documentary evidence within 60 days of delivery, though an extension may be granted.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss tax authorities impose a severe clawback regime for fraudulent export zero-rating claims. If the SFTA determines that export documentation was falsified or the goods did not leave Switzerland, the zero rating is retroactively reversed and VAT at the standard rate (8.1%) becomes due, plus interest. An additional penalty of up to three times the evaded tax (Art. 70-74 VAT Act) may be levied, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud under Art. 186-187 Swiss Federal Act on Administrative Criminal Law can result in fines up to CHF 100,000 or imprisonment for individuals. The statute of limitations for prosecution is 15 years for fraudulent claims, and ordinary assessments have a 10-year limitation period for wilful concealment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) in conjunction with the Federal Department of Finance and the State Secretariat for International Financial Affairs (SIF); no dedicated foreign exchange administration authority exists in Switzerland.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full capital and current account convertibility. The Swiss franc (CHF) is a freely convertible global reserve currency with no exchange controls. Foreign investors may freely inject, repatriate, and remit profits subject to standard Swiss corporate and tax laws. Profit remittance hurdles are essentially nil from a currency perspective; however, Swiss withholding tax of 35% on dividend distributions applies, reduced under applicable double taxation treaties upon proper filings. Capital gains from the sale of participation interests are generally non-taxable for foreign investors holding less than 5% of the company's capital, while intercompany loans must respect thin capitalization, interest rate arm's length, and substance requirements to avoid classification as hidden equity distribution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion regime for export receipts. Exporters are free to retain, deploy, or convert all proceeds in any currency, and there is no prescribed repatriation timeline. The only relevant obligations are commercial bookkeeping and tax reporting in CHF or functional currency, plus transparency and anti-money-laundering filing requirements for large or suspicious cross-border transactions under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Suisse AG (now integrated into UBS AG)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border EMI viability is Low-Medium. A Switzerland-licensed fintech company (FINMA 'FinTech' or 'Banking Innovator' license) or a full banking license is required for deposit-taking and payment intermediation. Offshore digital EMI licenses (e.g., UK, Lithuanian, or Singapore EMIs) do not carry any Swiss passporting rights and cannot provide regulated account-opening or payment collection services directly into Switzerland. They may be used solely as unregulated payment-off-ramp service providers with contractual disclaimers, subject to Swiss AMLA requirements; in practice, a Swiss AG should engage only FINMA-supervised payment institutions or licensed banks to maintain treasury credibility and avoid anti-money-laundering red flags.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not generally mandated under Swiss AMLA for low-risk corporate clients; however, most tier-1 Swiss banks require at least one senior director or beneficial owner to complete a physical or secure video-identification KYC interview for medium- to high-risk profiles such as data-scraping API commerce. Remote opening is legally permissible via video identification and electronic signature under Swiss banking practice, but the bank retains residual discretion. For a CHF AG with non-resident directors and an ISIC 6201 commercial scraping business that has no statutory license trigger, banks will typically impose a board resolution, apostilled certificate of incorporation, and a formal in-person or video call with the UBO or director plus, in many cases, a local Swiss resident director or registered agent mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk cross-border payment flows from data-scraping clients and proxy API resellers with unclear end-customer identity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML-compliant client onboarding pack including: (i) registered commercial register excerpt issued by the Swiss Commercial Register Office within 90 days; (ii) articles of incorporation confirming lawful ISIC 6201 data-processing activities; (iii) audited or management-prepared source-of-funds documentation showing commercial revenue correlation; (iv) detailed transaction-flow narratives and subcontractor agreements; (v) final-beneficial-owner registers and directors' passports; (vi) sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media screening results; (vii) a Swiss AMLA-compliant risk assessment and compliance manual; (viii) Swiss data-protection impact assessment for scraping/personal-data ingestion; and (ix) copies of all outward-facing API proxy agreements mapping end-customers to third-party risk tiers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency treasury participation (USDC) as an alternative payment rail without a regulated banking partner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documentation showing that USDC receipts are converted promptly via a FINMA-regulated Swiss crypto-bank or SRO-member financial intermediary; a treasury policy limiting crypto balances to operational float; a complete chain-of-title ledger for all wallet addresses; commercial invoices referring to the specific data-pipeline deliverable; and proof that all crypto transactions are covered by the Swiss AMLA obligations of the banking partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident controlling shareholders with hidden UBO structure through complex holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified share-register excerpts with direct and indirect beneficial ownership identification to natural-person level; notarized and apostilled board and shareholder resolutions; a written group-structure chart with jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction substance explanation; tax residence certificates for all intermediate entities; and an undertaking to provide quarterly UBO re-confirmations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity and large aggregated receipts inconsistent with an SME treasury profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Forward-looking cash-flow forecast signed by the CFO/board; contractual pipeline for expected scraper-API licensing volumes; evidence of dedicated reseller and merchant agreements; historical income statement and trial balance proving revenue pattern; and an explanation of any netting, batch settlement, or multi-currency lag that creates large intraday balances.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection into the Swiss AG is executed by international wire transfer over SWIFT using a compliant equity-contribution purpose code (e.g., 'CAPITAL' or 'TREATY/GENA' dependent on corridor) with a reference to the Swiss Commercial Register number, accompanied by the corporate board resolution and bank KYC pack. The receiving Swiss bank will typically request a copy of the cash-issuance resolution, the notarial deed if the share capital increase is registered, and the source-of-funds documentation for the foreign sender. CHF capital contributions up to CHF 20,000 are duty-exempt; amounts above that incur a 1% Swiss stamp duty, although contributions resulting in at least a 10% equity stake of a newly formed AG qualify for the participation relief/exemption where applicable. Wires must reference the client-specific escrow account if funds are held pending registration or conversion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for data-pipeline licensing, subcontractor settlements, and procurement are executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for direct invoice payments and SWIFT MT202 COV bank-to-bank transfers where intermediary clearing is required. Commercial letters of credit are permissible and standard for high-value international trade contracts but are less relevant for SaaS/data-API licensing; payment factories may use MT101 bulk instructions for repetitive vendor payment runs. The Swiss SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) rail settles all domestic and CHF-denominated transactions in real-time; EUR payments are cleared through SEPA or EURO SIC; USD payments require a correspondent bank. Regulatory verification requires the purpose code (e.g., dated, based on Swiss National Bank balance-of-payments classification) and maintenance of a payment file for Swiss AMLA audit requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic currency exposure
Cross-currency swaps for long-dated commercial contracts
FX options (European-style) for hedging uncertain deal flows
Vanilla currency swaps with settlement netting covered by an ISDA master agreement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax declaration for federal direct tax and cantonal/communal taxes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration; Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) for federal direct tax collection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Varies by canton; generally within 30 days of service of the tax return form and by the cantonal statutory date, commonly falling between 31 March and 31 August for prior-year tax declarations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest and administrative fines up to CHF 10,000; tax may be assessed at the administration's discretion; prolonged non-payment or non-filing may lead to forced execution and bankruptcy proceedings but not administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT return and settlement for Swiss value added tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration, VAT Division (ESTV/AFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The taxable period is the calendar year; periodic quarterly VAT returns are due within 60 days after the end of each quarter, and the final annual VAT return is due within 60 days after 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at the FTA rate; procedural fines up to CHF 10,000; intentional VAT evasion may trigger a surcharge of up to three times the evaded tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting and adoption of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and general meeting; minutes retained at the registered office; no filing with the commercial register unless capital or governance changes arise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date, e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A shareholder may apply to court to compel the meeting; directors may face civil liability for delay and, in insolvency situations, criminal liability for late bankruptcy filing; there is no administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer social security wage declaration and annual salary statements (AHV/IV/EO/ALV and occupational pension basis)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Central Compensation Office (ZAS/CAS) and the applicable compensation or pension fund
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage certificates must reach employees by 31 January of the following year; the employer's social security annual declaration is due as directed by the compensation office, typically by 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on late contributions; administrative fines and possible criminal sanction for false statements; no direct corporate strike-off consequence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and, where applicable, commercial register updates for director, share capital, or address changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canton of registration Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt); company records at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Changes must be filed with the commercial register within 30 days of the event; a best-practice annual verification is performed at the AGM and completed before the annual tax declaration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register mandatory changes may draw cantonal fines and, if knowingly false declarations are made, criminal liability; no changes means no filing is due.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit is mandatory for listed companies and systemically important financial institutions. A limited review audit is mandatory for an AG exceeding two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: CHF 20 million total assets, CHF 40 million net turnover, or 250 average full-time employees. A private AG below these thresholds may completely opt out of audit if it employs no more than 10 full-time equivalents and all shareholders consent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations, Arts. 957–962a, statutory accounting provisions; consolidated accounts of listed companies must comply with Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS; unlisted AGs may adopt IFRS voluntarily.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not require a public annual UBO confirmation filing. The AG must maintain an ongoing share register and, for bearer shares, a register of beneficial owners; share transfers become effective when recorded. AMLA-regulated intermediaries must verify beneficial ownership when establishing business relationships, and the company must update beneficial-owner data without undue delay after relevant changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book for shareholders' and board meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 – USD 5,500 per year for registered-office and administrative agent services in Zurich, Geneva, or Zug
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 30,000 for a statutory limited audit of a small to medium-size AG; ordinary audit of a non-listed digital data/API company generally ranges from USD 25,000 – USD 60,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal direct tax: 8.5% of net profit after tax (equivalent to 7.83% on pre-tax income; Art. 68 DBG). Combined federal + cantonal + municipal headline rates range from approximately 11.9% (Zug) to 21.1% (Zurich); Geneva approximately 13.99%; nationwide average approximately 15%. The applicable headline rate depends on the AG's registered seat.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (STAF, in force 2020): patent box granting up to 90% relief on qualifying IP income; R&D super-deduction of up to 150% of qualifying Swiss R&D labour and research costs; cantonal notional interest deduction; participation relief effectively exempting qualifying dividend and capital-gain income (Art. 69 DBG); de minimis threshold of CHF 20,000; OECD Pillar Two Qualified Domestic Top-Up Tax of 15% effective 1 January 2024 for MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss harmonised Cantonal Corporate Income Tax Return for Legal Entities (joint federal direct tax and cantonal/municipal ordinary tax assessment, Art. 39 ff. VStG, Art. 119-126 DBG), filed via the cantonal e-filing system (e.g., Zurich 'eSteuern', Zug 'TaxOnline', Geneva 'SIP') or the FTA 'eTax/SwissTax' portal for federal direct tax; annexes: audited or reviewed annual financial statements, tax reconciliation of non-deductible expenses and tax-exempt income, and transfer pricing documentation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Cantonal law generally requires submission within 3 to 6 months after fiscal year-end; extensions to 30 September (occasionally to 31 December) of the following calendar year are routinely granted for commercial taxpayers; missing a final deadline triggers default assessment (Ermessensveranlagung).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A1 – Jahresgewinn / annual net profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit per commercial balance sheet (Art. 958 OR) before tax allocation; taken directly from the audited income statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The AG is resident at its registered seat or place of effective management (Art. 50 DBG) and is taxed on worldwide income; the foreign parent's residence does not alter this line. If the foreign parent effectively manages the AG from abroad, the AG's seat may be reclassified, triggering deemed migration and exit-tax consequences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible expenses: federal and cantonal income taxes; excess interest on hybrid debt; 50% of supervisory board compensation; excessive management fees; hidden profit distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For foreign-owner groups, service fees, royalties and interest paid to the parent are deductible only if supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing evidence; unsupported items are recharacterised as hidden distribution and attract 35% withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A3 – Tax-exempt income and participation relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct qualifying participation income: dividends and capital gains from qualifying holdings of at least 10% of paid-up capital held for one year or more; deduct foreign PE results and foreign real estate income under applicable DTA provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Participation relief applies only to the Swiss resident entity and is independent of the beneficial owner's residence; the foreign shareholder separately claims DTA credits in its home jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A4 – Taxable profit before loss offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit plus add-backs minus exemptions and participation relief; constitutes the base for federal, cantonal and municipal income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company with a Swiss permanent establishment uses the same reconciliation but only for Swiss-source attributable income; a Swiss resident AG with foreign shareholders must report worldwide turnover without a territorial limitation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset prior-year losses within the 7-year carryforward window (Art. 67 DBG; Art. 25 StHG); no carryback; no group or fiscal-transparency relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the foreign shareholder cannot be transferred to the AG; Swiss law does not permit group relief even where the foreign parent consolidates the AG's results.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B – Taxable capital (cantonal capital tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cantonal and municipal capital tax base: paid-in share capital plus disclosed and hidden reserves, reduced by participation relief within capital tax and thin-capitalisation safe harbours (commonly 6:1 debt-to-equity ratio).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No federal capital tax; shareholder loans to the AG are reclassified as taxable capital where the ratio of related-party debt to equity exceeds Swiss FTA benchmarks or interest is not at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal direct tax: taxable profit times 8.5% computed on the net-of-tax basis per Art. 68 DBG; cantonal/municipal tax: taxable profit times cantonal base rate times communal multiplier.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The AG is separately assessed; non-resident shareholders receive no Swiss tax credit for the AG's corporate income tax except under an applicable DTA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: per-cantonal surcharge of up to 10% of assessed tax plus default interest (Art. 132-136 DBG); procedural non-compliance: fine up to CHF 10,000 (Art. 174 DBG); intentional evasion: fine equal to the evaded tax (Art. 175 DBG); aggravated evasion through false documents: fine between 100% and 300% of evaded tax and imprisonment up to 3 years (Art. 176 DBG); repeated non-compliance may lead to director disqualification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss VAT return (Mehrwertsteuerabrechnung) filed electronically through the Federal Tax Administration's 'ePortal / MWST-Abrechnung online'; applicable because API subscription and scraping services are taxable supplies (Art. 18 MWSTG); exports of digital services to foreign business customers are zero-rated where the recipient's place of business is abroad.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly (standard); annual return permitted where net turnover is below CHF 500,000
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: VAT return and payment due within 60 days after the end of each quarter or calendar year; extension only with prior FTA authorisation; repeated defaults trigger a fixed reminder procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic B2B and B2C recurring subscription and metered API revenue taxed at the standard Swiss VAT rate of 8.1%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When invoicing foreign-resident business customers, the place-of-supply rule (Art. 23 MWSTG) places the supply abroad: zero-rated, no Swiss VAT; the invoice must state the foreign recipient and show no Swiss tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Zero-rated exports of digital services to foreign B2B customers supported by evidence of the recipient's foreign administration (residence certificate, VAT registration number, commercial documentation).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No Swiss VAT liability on exported digital services; the foreign customer applies reverse-charge in the destination jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Input VAT on Swiss hosting, infrastructure, legal and advisory costs; pro-rata recovery where mixed use occurs; no deduction for entertainment expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Service charges invoiced to the AG by the foreign parent without Swiss VAT may still support input deduction; if the supplying parent is foreign, the AG must apply the reverse-charge mechanism (Bezugsteuer) where required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Warning then fine up to CHF 8,000 for late or incomplete returns (Art. 103 MWSTG); false declaration or concealment of turnover: fine up to CHF 20,000 plus retroactive tax and delay interest; VAT evasion: fine up to four times the evaded tax and imprisonment up to one year (Art. 105 MWSTG); responsible directors are jointly subject to criminal process under Art. 104 and 106 MWSTG.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% on gross dividend distributions (Art. 1 and 4 VStG) levied at the Swiss payor level; the tax is economically borne by the shareholder and is refunded, in whole or in part, only upon a documented claim or under a treaty-stipulated at-source relief procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Step 1: withhold 35% at distribution. Step 2: foreign shareholder files a refund claim with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) on Form 854/854-A for DTA countries (or Form 820/TV for the EU-Swiss agreement, which permits 0% for EU parent companies holding at least 10% for two years). Step 3: attach the original dividend coupon and a Form 823/854-B Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's tax authority within the previous three months, evidencing beneficial ownership. Step 4: refund processing takes 3 to 12 months. Under the Switzerland-China DTA (1990), the dividend rate is capped at 5% where the Chinese beneficial-owner company holds at least 10% of the share capital and at 10% for portfolio holdings; the Chinese shareholder must prove continuous beneficial ownership for the 365-day holding test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss domestic law imposes no withholding tax on ordinary loan interest or on royalty/licence fees paid to non-residents; the 35% anticipation tax applies only to interest on taxable bonds or book-entry securities issued by a Swiss issuer (Art. 4 VStG). Under the Switzerland-China DTA, source-tax limits are 10% for interest (Art. 11) and 10% for royalties (Art. 12); because Swiss domestic law imposes no tax, interest and royalties may be paid free of Swiss withholding, subject to the beneficial-owner and principal-purpose test and to transfer pricing documentation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration expects a Local File for cross-border controlled transactions (services, goods, financing, royalties) where cumulative related-party volume exceeds CHF 5,000,000 per fiscal year; a Master File applies where the foreign parent group has consolidated turnover of at least CHF 900,000,000 (2019 FTA transfer pricing documentation guidance); secondary adjustments are routinely applied where hidden distributions are found.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: TNMM (transactional net margin method) – most appropriate for API gateway and data-pipeline services
